en: When you're fine-tuning a model,
there are
mainly 2 ways of doing that. One would be to
overwrite all the parameters and weights
that were derived during pre-training and
maybe previous fine-tuning
with new parameters and weights.
This is quite complex and expensive because
it in the end means that you are retraining
the entire model.
The more efficient form of fine-tuning is
the so-called LoRA
or parameter efficient fine-tuning approach,
also called PEFT. LoRA stands for Low-Rank
Adaptation. Now, what's the idea here? The
idea is that we're talking about fine-tuning
and you're taking a large language model or
a small language model, which again are kind
of the same. It's just a different amount of
parameters.
And you're adding your own data. You're
using a fine-tuning tool
and you're then not replacing the original
parameters. And instead you can think of
attaching extra layers to that model with
new parameters and weights that have a great
impact on the outcome. Therefore, it's much
cheaper because you're leaving the original
model, the original neural network as it is,
and you're just adding more to it, but such
that it has a true impact. And that's
therefore the predominant way of fine-tuning
models, for example, inside of companies,
because it's way faster and cheaper and
nonetheless gives you highly specific models
that you can purpose-build for your specific
use cases.
